lead: she stopped speaking to you eleven years ago and the friendship did not stop. it runs on privately, in detail, most weeks, and neither she nor anybody you live with has been told it exists.
sun: retrieval does not need the other end to be there. the number still works, the argument is still in progress, the answer you would give her now is current and revised, and none of it requires her participation, which is exactly why it has lasted eleven years. other people keep a lapsed thing as a memory. you keep it running, one-sided, at working temperature, and it costs you nothing to do.
moon: the covering goes on before any decision to conceal. a thing forms and the cover is over it the same afternoon, so no evening has ever existed on which you chose not to say it. one upright holds all of it, and the upright is that nobody has been shown in. say one sentence out loud and the cover is off for good.
pull: eleven years of a friendship that ended, kept running by one person in a room with no second occupant, and the only thing holding the cover up is that it has never been described.
tension: you are the one who takes things well, and everybody who has lived with you would swear to it. there is nothing to catch: a thing that never reaches the surface leaves no trace of not reaching it. so the closest position anybody holds is beside somebody genuinely calm and genuinely present, and the eleven-year distance between that person and the one keeping the interior has no words either of you could open it with.
cost: holding a thing at full strength for a decade with no witness costs you nothing: no reassurance required, nothing thinning for want of an audience, no evening on which it had to be justified. what is never shown is never corrected. she has had eleven years to revise the version of her you keep, and no route by which to do it, and nor has anyone else in there.

lead: two of the people this household is organised around have not slept in it for years. the room is kept, the money is worked out with them in it, and the three who actually live here have never been asked.
sun: nobody comes off the roll. a person who moved out is a person elsewhere, so the house stays sized for the whole list: the bed made up, the chair carried in at the big meals, a share of each year's arithmetic set against an arrival nobody can date. one of them was gone six years and walked in on a tuesday to a room that was ready, and that settles it for another decade.
moon: none of this is sentimental. an enclosure gets built to dimensions, and the ones who left are dimensions here, structural, sized into the plan instead of missed on birthdays. nobody indoors thinks about where a measurement came from. so three people run a whole domestic life inside a shape taken off a roll that has never lost a name, and it reads to them as the way a house is.
pull: the place is kept at the size of everybody who has ever lived in it. three people are indoors tonight, and not one of them set a single dimension.
tension: the objection has a shape nobody in a family can get their mouth around. asking for the room means proposing that a person be struck off, in a house where he is still counted. so it arrives as a row about storage, or about money, from a daughter who has been reasonable for eleven years and can no longer say what she is not being reasonable about. sentimental gets used about you, and nothing in the arrangement is memorial.
cost: somebody who left this house can walk in on a wednesday to a place set for them, with nothing required at the door, and two people are alive because it was available at the hour. the ones who never went anywhere live to terms set by the ones who did, and there is no way to ask for more room that is not a request to remove a name.

lead: he went under in the second year, and you did the four years again with him from the start. two others have had a second run at it, and he is now on his third.
sun: the release at the boundary is genuine. you go home, you keep no line on anybody, none of them owes you a call. the road behind them never gets taken up. it stays passable in both directions, so a man who comes apart four years on has nothing to apply for and nothing to explain, and you meet him where he fell and start walking. a first crossing is the part everybody else performs.
moon: your part finishes at the boundary and does not include the country. what you have of these nine is the walking and nothing else: no idea what a good year of theirs looks like, no picture of any of them at ease. for three, there is no far side. they arrive, go quiet while it holds, and the friendship resumes at the point where the ground gives way.
pull: you take them to the border and go home, and then you come for them again, and the three who know that has happened before have never had to make an arrival hold.
tension: his family settled on an account in which he has had every chance and you are the reason he is not dead, and both halves of that are accurate. the sentence they never reach is the one with the road in it: a way passable in both directions is a way out of an arrival as much as into one. nobody can put that in a room where the only person turning up is the one it lands on.
cost: few people can watch four years of work come apart and turn up at the bottom with nothing withheld and nothing said about the last time, so anyone who has used up everyone's patience has one route left. the count cannot be closed. a crossing can always be reopened, so none of the nine is finished, and which of them got there is a question your record cannot answer.

lead: the person you were at nineteen has never been retired. that one is on the far end of a length you are still holding, and the pull comes from down there as often as it comes from you.
sun: nothing in your life converts into a phase. what you wanted at twenty-two is retrievable this afternoon, at strength, so it never got demoted into a story about somebody you used to be: the undertaking given then is still in force, the taste is intact, the quarrel is live. everyone else earns a former self by leaving it far enough away to describe. yours has never got that far off.
moon: and a cord does its work only while both ends pull. that end pulls. the nineteen-year-old has views on the current arrangement and gets them heard, at full weight, in rooms nobody that age has sat in. it is also why you do not drift: a length under tension from both directions holds a straight line, and people who have known you forty years can predict you to the week.
pull: you are one continuous length, end to end, with no part of it that can be cut out. the year everybody agreed to forget is on the same piece as the good decade.
tension: anyone else gets to say that was a different person and be believed. offered the same line, you decline it, and the declining reads as modesty or as something wrong with you. the amnesty is unavailable in both directions, and what follows is a supply problem: there is no segment available to leave out, so the whole run arrives wherever you do, delivered early and accurately to people who would have preferred the short version.
cost: a promise taken on at twenty holds at fifty at the original strength, usually to somebody who has forgotten making the other half of it, so people let go by everybody find one attachment still under load. the same continuity keeps whatever should have lapsed. a cord ends by being cut, and a cut anywhere takes the whole length with it, so nothing about you gets revised in one place.
